text: Figure 5.50: A CompuMethod and its attributes define data semantics This is obviously a lot safer than the opposite approach where a given physical/internal value would first be converted to its internal/physical equivalent and then, after the con- version is finished there would be (as a second step) the obligation to check whether the result of the conversion is actually valid in terms of the applicable limits. As hinted by [TPS_SWCT_01548], the definition of valid intervals is done by means of specifying the valid intervals as opposed to specifying the invalid intervals . This observation is also valid for uses of CompuMethod outside the scope of this document.
